No—almost certainly not with unaided eyesight.

Although the Moon is geometrically above the horizon, it is only **0.09% illuminated** and just **3.45° from the Sun**. At a low altitude of about **10.5°**, atmospheric extinction further reduces its already tiny crescent, while the nearby daylight sky is extremely bright. The Moon is also only about **2.6° from the Sun in azimuth**, making attempts to search for it optically unsafe.

This is an exceptionally young crescent—effectively at the limit even for carefully controlled telescopic imaging. An ordinary observer would not see it in bright daylight. **Do not use binoculars or a telescope**, because the Sun is dangerously close to the line of sight. Wait until a later date, when the Moon is farther from the Sun and visible after sunset.
